newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 5.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Monday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* Main share index is likely to hover around the 2,600 support level on the lack of positive news to prop up the market, traders said.

* Release of the April inflation figure and listing of movie production firm Premiere Entertainment Production are not expected to propel the market to higher ground, said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities.
* BPI Securities Corp said in its weekly outlook that short-lived rallies may be seen on issues which have reached bargain levels.
* On Friday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index fell 42.52 points to 2,605.65.
* On Friday, the Dow Jones rose 94.72 points to 7,071.20. PLDT's ADR gained $0 1/4 to $55 1/4.

* The Philippine government is set to propose to Congress a 541 billion peso national budget for 1998, 10 percent bigger than the 1997 appropriated budget which provides for a 16 billion peso surplus, up from the 14.7 billion surplus targeted this year.

* The Central Bank said the Philippines' foreign exchange reserves rose to $11.82 billion as of April 15, up from $11.75 billion at the end of 1996. The Bank said the reserves are at a comfortable level enabling the bank to intervene effectively in the foreign exchange market.
* Premiere Entertainment Production will list 520 million common shares to cover the initial public offering of 180 million shares at an offer price of one peso apiece.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the presidential palace has directed the Department of Trade and Industry, Department of Finance and the Securities and Exchange Commission to conduct separate studies of the investment climate which may have led to the pullout of foreign funds from the stock market.
* BusinessWorld reported that the Central Bank sees the inflation rate in April at 4.7 percent from 4.8 percent in March.

* Manila Bulletin said the Manila Electric Co will buy the 1,500-megawatt output from a mothballed nuclear power station in Bataan, south of Manila by the year 2004 and not by 2002 as expected by seller state-run National Power Corp.

* Manila Times said Jollibee Foods Corp's directors approved last week a proposal for the retail fastfood firm to invest in a 50 percent stake in a local holding company that will issue warrants and other instruments based on shares of Jollibee.
* The peso closed lower at 26.374 to the dollar vs 26.37.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average rose to 11.0625 percent from 10.28125 percent.
